summary: A 1933 Forest Service L-4 summit cabin in Olympic National Park, used for aircraft warning in WWII and rebuilt on its foundation in 2017 after years of decline.

facts.design: Single-story frame cab, 14x14 ft L-4 type, on a summit (no tower)

access.note: Hike-in only. A 2017 article says it is accessed only by the Long Ridge trail. An undated page says use is only for emergency purposes. No current park notice was found.

visit.trail_note: Long Ridge trail, given as 10 miles (Willhite Web) or 13 miles (NWHikers)

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service with an L-4 cab; materials packed in by horse
Aircraft Warning Service station in WWII. A 1944 report gives Oct 5, 1942 as the last day of service; a passage names lookouts Leith and Mary Johnson in 1943
Placed on the National Register of Historic Places July 13, 2007
Foundation rebuilt, siding and roof replaced, windows re-glazed; volunteers plus grants from Washington's National Park Fund and the REI Foundation

evidence.quote: This lookout features a 14'x14' L-4 cab and was built by the US Forest Service in 1933.
Clallam County, Washington
Olympic National Park

evidence.supports: materials packed by horse to summit in 1933
evidence.quote: The materials were packed by horses to the summit for the construction in 1933 of this L-4 cab.

evidence.supports: used as Aircraft Warning Service station
evidence.quote: It was also used as an Aircraft Warning Service station.

evidence.supports: 1944 report gives Oct 5, 1942 as last day
evidence.quote: Last day of service was October 5, 1942, the site was retained by the Park Service.

evidence.supports: lookouts in 1943 were Leith and Mary Johnson
evidence.quote: The AWS Lookouts in 1943 were Leith and Mary Johnson.
has been gradually failing for the last 15+years

evidence.supports: siding and roof replaced in 2017 repairs
evidence.quote: The siding was replaced and painted, a new cedar shingle roof was added
So far, the foundation has been rebuilt
Windows were re-glazed and painted, and the door was replaced.

evidence.quote: Dodger Point Lookout was restored in 2017 with the assistance of volunteers and grant funding from Washington's National Park Fund and the REI Foundation.

evidence.supports: fire finder and crank telephone remain inside
evidence.quote: The lookout still has its Osborne fire finder and crank telephone.

evidence.supports: Long Ridge is the most accessible route
evidence.quote: Two trails reach the location; the most accessible is Long Ridge.
Although this appropriate name fits the long 10 mile ridge trail

corrections.why: firelookout.com names Clallam County, Washington. The NHLR detail page spells it Challam County, which appears to be a typo carried into our record.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the end of the Aircraft Warning Service use. Willhite Web quotes a 1944 report saying the last day was Oct 5, 1942, but also names lookouts in 1943, and Wikipedia's article is cited for the WWII use without a date. Trail length conflicts (10 miles per Willhite Web, 13 miles per NWHikers). Elevation conflicts (NHLR 5,728 ft; firelookout 5,753 ft; the brief's 1745.9 m matches NHLR). Current public access is not confirmed; the Willhite page is undated. The NRHP number 07000736 comes from the brief, and the Wikipedia article gives the same number.
